title: Experimental Design B 2027
summary: Experimental Design has no written exam. Three students get an assigned topic, a set of materials they have never seen, fifty minutes, and a two-part report form scored against the official checklist. This course is that checklist, section by section, with the tiebreak order the rules give: analysis first, then procedure, variables, table, graph.
objectives: Turn an assigned topic and unknown materials into a testable problem statement and a reasoned hypothesis inside twenty minutes
Name the independent, dependent and controlled variables, and say what each uncontrolled variable would let in
Write a procedure and draw a set-up diagram another team could run from
Build a data table and a graph that score on format as well as content, and summarise trials with mean, median, mode and range
Write claim, evidence and reasoning, and state experimental error and limitations honestly

units.title: The First Twenty Minutes
units.summary: Twenty minutes to read a topic, see materials for the first time, design an experiment and start running it. The clock is the hardest constraint in the event.
objectives: Turn an assigned topic into a testable question
Get data collection started inside twenty minutes

lessons.title: From Assigned Topic to Statement of the Problem
lessons.objective: Write a statement of the problem that names both variables and is not answerable yes or no, from an assigned topic and an unknown materials set.

lessons.title: Writing a Hypothesis That Scores
lessons.objective: Write a hypothesis that predicts a direction of effect and gives a reason, rather than restating the question.
keywords: predicts a relationship between the IV
rationale is given for the hypothesis

lessons.title: Designing With Materials You Have Never Seen
lessons.objective: Inventory an unknown materials set and choose from it an independent variable you can actually vary at three or more levels.

lessons.title: Budgeting Twenty and Thirty Minutes
lessons.objective: Allocate the two event phases across design, trials and write-up so data collection starts early enough to repeat.

units.title: Variables
units.summary: Variables are their own checklist section and the third tiebreaker.
objectives: Name IV, DV and controlled variables for any experiment
Spot what a missing control lets in

lessons.title: The One You Change and the One You Measure
lessons.objective: Identify the independent and dependent variable in an experiment and state which axis each belongs on.

lessons.title: Controlled Variables, and Naming Enough of Them
lessons.objective: List the controlled variables for an experiment and explain what each one being uncontrolled would do to the result.

lessons.title: When Two Things Change at Once
lessons.objective: Identify a confounded design and explain why its result cannot be attributed to the independent variable.

lessons.title: Levels of the Independent Variable, and Repeats
lessons.objective: Choose at least three levels of the independent variable and enough repeated trials to show variation, and justify both.

units.title: Procedure and Set-Up Diagrams
units.summary: Second tiebreaker. The test is whether another team could run it from your words.
objectives: Write a procedure another team could follow exactly

lessons.title: A Procedure Somebody Else Could Follow
lessons.objective: Write a numbered procedure with quantities, distances and repetitions specified, and check it for steps only you would know.

lessons.title: The Set-Up Diagram
lessons.objective: Draw and label a set-up diagram showing the apparatus, where the measurement is taken and what is held constant.

lessons.title: Listing Materials Precisely
lessons.objective: Write a materials list with counts and dimensions, distinguishing what was provided from what was used.

lessons.title: Designing Something Safe Enough to Run
lessons.objective: Identify the safety considerations of a proposed design and state why a disqualifying design is not worth the points.

units.title: Data Tables, Graphs and Statistics
units.summary: Fourth and fifth tiebreakers, and the part most teams lose points on for formatting rather than for the science.
objectives: Build a data table with units and trials
Choose and label the right graph

lessons.title: Both Kinds of Observation
lessons.objective: Record qualitative and quantitative observations separately and explain what each contributes to the analysis.

lessons.title: A Data Table That Scores Full Marks
lessons.objective: Construct a data table with a title, labelled columns, units in the headers, every trial and a computed average.

lessons.title: Bar, Line or Scatter
lessons.objective: Choose the graph type that matches the data, and justify the choice from whether the independent variable is categorical or continuous.

lessons.title: Titles, Axes, Units and Scale
lessons.objective: Label a graph with a title, both axis names, units and an even scale, putting the independent variable on the x axis.

lessons.title: Mean, Median, Mode and Range
lessons.objective: Compute the mean, median, mode and range of a trial set and say which is the better summary when an outlier is present.

lessons.title: Describing What the Graph Shows
lessons.objective: Describe a trend in terms of direction and rate, and distinguish describing a trend from explaining it.

units.title: Claim, Evidence and Reasoning
units.summary: The first tiebreaker, and the section worth the most thought.
objectives: Write a claim backed by evidence and reasoning
State an error and a limitation honestly

lessons.title: Claim, Evidence, Reasoning
lessons.objective: Write an analysis that states a claim, cites specific data as evidence, and gives scientific reasoning connecting the two.

lessons.title: Saying the Hypothesis Was Not Supported
lessons.objective: State whether the data supported the hypothesis and explain why an unsupported hypothesis is not a failed experiment.

lessons.title: Naming Your Experimental Errors
lessons.objective: Identify specific sources of random and systematic error in the experiment just run, and say which direction each would push the result.

lessons.title: Limitations and What You Would Change
lessons.objective: State the limitations of the design and propose a specific improvement that would address a named limitation.
keywords: Suggestions to improve experiment with rationale

lessons.title: Application Beyond the Bench
lessons.objective: State a real-world application of the finding that follows from what was actually measured.
keywords: Applications and Recommendations for Further Use
